title: Your first Python program
examples: How do I make the computer say something?
What happens if I write the code wrong?
Can I print numbers or just words?

explain.say: Today we are learning to write our first Python program.
The print function tells the computer to display something.
To run code, you need a special coding environment.

draw.text: Run the code to see output

explain.say: When code runs, it gives us the expected result.
Sometimes the computer shows an error message. This is normal.
In real life, we use printing to show information to people.

faq.q: What is the difference between printing words and printing numbers?
faq.a: You must put words inside quotation marks like this. Numbers do not need those quotation marks around them.
asks: Do I use quotes for numbers?
How do I print text versus numbers?

faq.q: If my code gives an error, does that mean I failed?
faq.a: No, getting an error just means the computer needs help understanding you. It is part of learning to code.
asks: What should I do when the code breaks?

faq.q: What exactly does the print function do?
faq.a: The print function takes whatever you put inside its parentheses and shows it on the screen for you to see.
asks: What is the job of print?
How do I make the computer talk?

faq.q: Do I have to run the code to see anything?
faq.a: Yes, you must always run the code after writing it. Writing it is just like writing a recipe.

faq.q: What is the most common error when I start?
faq.a: A common mistake is forgetting the closing parenthesis or the quotation marks around text.
asks: What syntax mistake do beginners make?
Why do I get a syntax error?

facts: The print function displays output to the console.
Text data must always be enclosed in quotation marks.
Running code executes the instructions written in the program.
Errors are messages that help you fix your code.

quiz.say: To make the computer display the word Apple, what should you write?
quiz.why: You must use quotation marks around words so Python knows it is text.

wrong.1: Python thinks Apple is a variable name, not the word you want.
wrong.2: You are missing the opening quotation mark for the text.
wrong.3: The parentheses must wrap the entire command, including the quotes.

quiz.say: If you write print(5 + 3), what will the computer show?
quiz.why: Python sees the plus sign and calculates the math before printing the result.

wrong.0: Python reads this as printing the number 5, and then adding 3 separately.
wrong.1: The parentheses around the 3 are unnecessary here.
wrong.3: Putting quotes around it makes the computer print the symbols, not the answer.

quiz.say: If you forget the closing parenthesis, what kind of error might you see?
quiz.why: A SyntaxError means you broke the grammar rules of the Python language.

wrong.0: This is not a real error message; it describes a mistake in thinking, not code.
wrong.1: This error usually happens when you mix different types of data incorrectly.
wrong.3: This error happens when the code runs but encounters a problem during execution.
